items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Sharky's drummer was named Roy Montgomery. And he was Sharky's brother-in-law. Uh, nephew, rather. Their nephew.

ctx.x: All right, okay, it's going again. You were talking about Emmett Hardy and this band, Sharky and the Taunty.

Well, uh, somehow or other, they, uh, they had a run in with a club. It was a club, a social club that, uh, that had this. It was the Taunty Aiden Social Club. And they had this hall. And, uh, they had a run in, so they fired Sharky. And they hired Hardy, you see. So we went over there. And, uh, they had a bandstand. And the bandstand was against the back wall. And they had a window, like that. Right in the back of the drums. And in those days, there weren't any sense. The first thing is spurs, Bill. You know,…

So then we finally got out and we were going to catch the streetcars because we were all from over the river. And those days there was always a feud going on between the guys from Algiers and the guys from New Orleans, the guys from Gretna and the guys from New Orleans. Or even from one neighborhood to the other. And always about 15 of them got around us. They wanted to know what we were doing, taking a shorty job and everything like that. And they were just about getting ready to... They'd always send a little…
